text:
Zach: Ledgerly on support ticket #1248 reports that after the v3.2 rollout responses are missing required 'transaction_id' and include a spurious 'estimated_amount' field. They say it's breaking their ingestion. Rollout id r-2026-03-15-14. Can we rollback?
Maya: @Zach can you paste the failing example and a request id so we can repro quickly?
Zach: here's sample request id: req_0a9f1c. Before (v3.1):
```
{"transaction_id":"tx_77b3","status":"settled","amount":421.50}
```
After (v3.2):
```
{"status":"settled","estimated_amount":"~422","note":"derived from context"}
```
They're losing transaction_id entirely.
Evan: That's bad. What's canary percent? Any uptick in latency/errors?
Priya: Checked metrics: canary at 15% started 2026-03-15T14:02Z. No latency spike, 5xxs flat. But schema mismatch spikes in structured-output failure rate reported by Ledgerly and our regression eval runs.
Maya: OK we should revert the rollout to v3.1 for that route and run a quick cobbler test. Recommend immediate rollback for the 'json-structured' routing policy.
Priya: I can execute rollback. Command for hosted: 
```
redwoodctl rollout revert --id r-2026-03-15-14 --target-version v3.1 --force
```
For Dedicated/private customers we need to push routing override: 
```
redwoodctl routing override --route json-structured --model v3.1 --duration 30m
```
Zach: please do it, and I'll tell Ledgerly we're reverting and will monitor.
DeployBot: Deployment action started: revert r-2026-03-15-14 -> v3.1 by priya at 2026-03-15T14:18:10Z. Tracking id deploy-7862.
Priya: Revert executed, pushed override. Canaries should drain in ~2m. Monitoring now. @Evan please watch for logs matching req_0a9f1c.
Evan: Watching. I see new requests returning transaction_id again for that request id sample.
Lucy: I'll draft a short customer update: "We reverted to the previous model version while we investigate the schema change. No billing impact expected." Send me any nuances.
Maya: Postmortem owner? I'll take triage, Priya/Evan to investigate root cause (model behavior/regression vs conversion step), Zach/Sarah to coordinate customer comms., Lucy to finalize messaging.
IncidentBot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-17. Assigned: Maya. Severity: P1 (customer-visible regression).
Zach: Ledgerly confirms ingestion resumes after revert. They asked for ETA on fix and rollback window.
Maya: We'll run a focused eval comparing v3.1->v3.2 on structured-output prompt set. ETA 4 hours for first pass. We'll keep them updated every 30m. :thumbsup: 
Priya: Leaving routing override for 30m, then will either lift or re-pin depending on findings. Logging capture enabled for schema fields.
Lucy: I'll send a note to account with the revert details and expected follow-up.
Maya: Thanks team. Action items: (1) Priya rollback + keep override, (2) Evan + Maya run targeted evals and logs, (3) Zach+Sarah customer comms, (4) Lucy draft account note. Reopen if rollback doesn't stabilize.
Zach: Ack. Closing loop once postmortem doc ready.
